correctness.rationale: For x nonzero let t=N(x), u=N(F_a(x)), c=Tr(a), d=N(a). Independence of 1,a and a²=ca−d make F_a²(x)=x equivalent to t+u+c=0 and tu=d+1. These force t²+ct+d=−1, so the norm recursion gives u=−t and hence c=0. Conversely c=0 and t²=−d−1 imply the two equations. Trace zero is impossible for outsiders in characteristic two; otherwise a²=−d is a nonsquare, so a²−1 is nonzero and has two distinct nonzero square roots exactly in the stated case. The corresponding fibers have q+1 points each and are exchanged; 0 is the unique fixed point because a=1−N(x) would put a in K. Independently, the conic s²−t²=1 has q−1 points by factoring, so sum_t χ(t²+1)=−1. There are 1+χ(−1) zeros of t²+1, and therefore (q−χ(−1))/2 values of t where it is a nonsquare, all t≠0. Pairing ±t and taking the two outsider square roots of each t²+1 gives the same number of active coefficients. Zieve's exact permutation parameters have trace 3μ≠0 for q≡2 mod 3 and trace zero in characteristic three; any nonzero base-field coefficient would kill the norm fiber N(x)=−a, so no permutation cases were dropped. The packaged verification/verify_cycles.py was inspected, not executed: its main loops test fixed and exact two-period counts on explicit finite fields and compare exponentiation on a subset, not permutation necessity or all prime powers. Its header mentions a stale filename; RESULT.md gives the actual replay path.

value.rationale: This classifies the first nontrivial periodic orbits of a known norm-lift family even outside the bijective cases. It identifies the exact fibers and their exchange, and quantifies how many parameters exhibit it, splitting a family whose prior bijectivity classification does not distinguish these dynamics. The result is uniform in the field and goes beyond a small-field cycle check.
